findings.description: Materially changed findings can be classified as PERSISTED by F001 because clearance accounting is by finding_id, while F002 only defines convergence behavior for new findings. That leaves invalidated dispositions without a clearly blocking policy path when the same semantic id recurs with a different fingerprint.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit changed_prior_ids or materially_changed finding accounting to the ledger and make the policy treat invalidated changed findings as blocking until re-disposition or fresh clearance.

findings.description: F006 derives same-cell ordinals by sorting content fingerprints, but insertion, removal, or content edits inside a multi-finding cell can renumber otherwise related findings. That undermines the stable finding_id contract used by clearance accounting, disposition binding, and ledger reconstruction.
findings.recommendation: Define stable cross-round matching semantics for multi-finding cells, or explicitly make cell-level invalidation replace per-finding stability for those cells and reflect that in F001 clearance accounting.

findings.description: F001 says the rounds ledger is appended only when the auditor actually runs, while F003 requires legacy override usage to be logged in the rounds ledger. A lock pass using the override may not run the auditor, so the write target and append rules conflict.
findings.recommendation: Resolve whether non-auditor events are allowed in the rounds ledger, or move override usage to a separate append-only lock events artifact referenced by the ledger.

findings.description: F002 includes advisory findings in the operator_disposition_required branch, but also states advisory findings never hard-block on their own. The plan does not define whether advisory-only rounds proceed, require disposition, or are ignored when mixed with medium or low findings.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit policy rows for advisory-only and advisory-mixed rounds, including whether advisory findings require dispositions during no-auditor resolution.

findings.description: The disposition CLI records against finding ids, but the lock refusal contract only promises to name the policy branch. It does not require surfacing the exact finding ids, fingerprints, classes, and allowed disposition kinds the operator must act on.
findings.recommendation: Require lock refusals to emit a machine-readable disposition_required list with finding_id, fingerprint, class, severity, allowed disposition kinds, and required reason or follow-up fields.

findings.description: The convergence policy says it can proceed, but the acceptance criteria do not explicitly cover the case where the latest round fully clears prior findings and produces zero current findings. That is the cleanest successful convergence case and should be pinned.
findings.recommendation: Add a zero-finding latest-round branch that proceeds without disposition or paid calls, and test it through both the pure policy and plan lock path.
